hook.text: A jet engine's gas temperature exceeds the melting point of its blades — the coating makes survival possible.

buildup.text: Thermal barrier coatings are ceramic layers (yttria-stabilized zirconia) sprayed onto metal blades.

discovery.text: The ceramic insulates the metal — dropping surface temperature by 100–300°C across a 0.5 mm layer.

twist.text: Thermal cycling causes the coating to crack and spall — matching expansion between ceramic and metal is critical.

climax.text: Every modern jet engine uses TBCs — they're why gas temperatures can exceed alloy melting points.

punchline.text: A thin ceramic blanket lets metal survive temperatures that should melt it.

quiz.question: What do thermal barrier coatings do?
options: They increase the metal's melting point
They insulate the metal surface, reducing temperature by 100–300°C
